items.title: Police charge man with murdering five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby in Alice Springs
items.description: NT police charge Jefferson Lewis with murdering the girl, who disappeared from the Old Timers/Ilyperenye town camp last weekend.

items.title: After Little Baby's death, Canavan demands government stop 'running scared'
items.description: Nationals leader Matthew Canavan says after the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby, the government must "move on" from its defeat at the Voice referendum and re-engage on Indigenous policy debate.

items.title: Three dead, man arrested after violent incident at home in Sydney
items.description: Police say three people who have died after a "grizzly" incident at a home in Sydney's south-west overnight were members of the same family.

items.title: It just cost $2,553 to fill up 'Whiskers' — and Australians might bear the cost
items.description: On Australia's busiest freight route, it takes four shots of coffee, $2,553 of fuel and a little hair metal to keep the wheels of the economy turning.

items.title: A year after the landslide, Albanese faces a harsher reality
items.description: The prime minister's second term is now defined less by what he wants to do than by what unforeseen events will allow.

items.title: 'Inhumane': Mick's disgust at cops' justification over the tasering of his 95yo mum
items.description: In an in-depth interview ahead of the inquest into his mother Clare Nowland's nursing home death, Mick says the family wants changes that will prevent another tragedy.

items.title: The cafe meeting, the $2m bounty and the botched hit that shocked Sydney
items.description: As the house of Hamzy began to fall one of its senior members hatched a million-dollar plan to take out rivals in revenge. What followed has been a secret for five years.

items.title: Live: Trump says resuming strikes in Iran 'a possibility'
items.description: The US president told reporters he is reviewing a new peace proposal from Iranian negotiators. Follow live.

items.title: 'I made the choice': Why James Valentine resolved to die on his own terms
items.description: Broadcaster James Valentine was offered two different treatments for his cancer, so he chose the one that let him keep doing what he loved. Australian Story followed Valentine over his final 12 months as he faced the end with courage, purpose and humour.

items.title: 'If the cops came, you'd slip out the back': The shifting role of Aussie pubs
items.description: From a tiny Riverina pub to a polished inner-city institution, Australia's local pubs are changing hands at record pace. As big money pours in, what happens to the communities that built them?

items.title: Liberals focus on 'lessons' for Victorian election after decisive Nepean win
items.description: It took less than three hours from the start of vote counting for election analysts to call the result in the Liberals' favour, with a win for former local mayor Anthony Marsh.

items.title: They escaped scam compounds then saw their suffering 'gamified'
items.description: Scam centre survivors say they are hurt by games that serialise scam compound experiences online, but one creator says he hopes people find the game "fun".

items.title: Australian says Gaza aid boat activists were beaten by Israeli navy
items.description: Zack Schofield was one of three Australians taken to hospital after being released by Israeli authorities, and says he saw at least 10 of his crew being shot by rubber bullets.

items.title: King Charles won over Trump with his visit but not Zohran Mamdani
items.description: King Charles's US state visit hit a bump in New York when Mayor Zohran Mamdani said if the pair were to speak, he would "probably encourage him to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond".

items.title: 'Soundtrack to Australia': ARIA reveals six 2026 Hall of Fame inductees
items.description: For the first time in more than a decade, multiple artists are being inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame.

items.title: It's your Sunday serve of stumpers in our spelling quiz
items.description: You lot take your spelling seriously. Repeat after me: It's just an internet quiz. It's just an internet quiz.

items.title: A 17-year-old Go-Betweens song inspired Robert Forster's debut novel
items.description: The Go-Betweens frontman spent years developing the story, which follows a pair of musicians on the run from the law as they try to clear their names.

items.title: Murray-Darling Basin's apex predator back from the brink
items.description: Murray cod numbers have bounced back across much of Victoria and NSW, and that's good news for the whole Murray-Darling Basin ecosystem.

items.title: Australian taxpayers take on risk for major oil and gas projects
items.description: Australian governments take on risk to get major resource projects up and running, so why don't they take an equity stake?

items.title: Piastri second in Miami sprint race before tough qualifying result
items.description: McLaren finally halts the Mercedes dominance with a one-two finish in the Miami sprint race, before a difficult qualifying session.

items.title: What a vote of confidence in NZ's prime minister could mean for the country's election
items.description: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has survived a vote of confidence in his leadership amid a drop in approval ratings. Here's what this could mean for NZ's upcoming election.

items.title: Backflip but no handshake as Ukrainian beats Russian at Madrid Open
items.description: Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk backflips after beating Russian Mirra Andreeva in the Madrid Open women's final.

items.title: Nomadic family says 'dream is more powerful' than surging fuel prices
items.description: While many Australians are thinking twice about big road trips due to fuel costs, the Sharavnyam family from Mongolia is determined to fulfil a dream to travel the world.

items.title: Beck spent decades as an alt-rock anomaly. Now he's going symphonic
items.description: The alt-rock anomaly has toured Australia numerous times over the past 30 years. But this month is his first accompanied by symphonic orchestras.

items.title: Calls for change after soccer club told it needs men's team to compete
items.description: Millicent United's women's side is flying this season, but without a men's team the club has been told they are unable to compete.
